_comment: Gold canonical K-IR propositions for Benchmark v0. Each is the target equivalence class that paraphrase 'variants' (variants.json) should collapse onto. 'context' fields are the conditions/assumptions that make the statement true -- they are the whole point of the benchmark. Revised per review round 1: fixed K015's LinearExtent->Volume bug, restricted K002/K003/K004 to defensible regimes instead of universal claims, split speed vs velocity in K012, added missing concept references.

propositions.nl_gloss: Voltage equals current times resistance (Ohm's law).
propositions.notes: Classic law-of-nature proposition; no differentiability subtleties.

propositions.nl_gloss: For an ordinary metal in the positive-temperature-coefficient regime, electrical resistance increases as temperature increases.
propositions.notes: dR/dT > 0 for most conducting metals (OpenStax), excluding special low-TCR alloys, phase transitions, and superconducting transitions. Deliberately paired with K003 to test context-sensitive relation classification (see P01: these should come out COMPATIBLE, not CONTRADICTS). Note the context is about a TRANSPORT REGIME, not an eternal property of 'Metal' as a class -- see C14's scope_note.

propositions.nl_gloss: For an intrinsic/lightly-doped semiconductor in the standard negative-temperature-coefficient regime, resistance decreases as temperature increases.
propositions.notes: dR/dT < 0, canonical example intrinsic silicon (OpenStax notes this sign depends on semiconductor type and doping level, so the claim is scoped to a concrete example rather than 'all semiconductors'). Surface-level negation of K002; correct system must classify K002/K003 as COMPATIBLE (shared MONOTONIC_* structure, disjoint transport-regime context), not CONTRADICTS.

propositions.nl_gloss: For an ordinary solid in the positive-thermal-expansion regime, linear dimensions increase as temperature increases, at constant pressure.

context.material_regime: ordinary_positive_expansion (excludes known negative-thermal-expansion solids, e.g. some zirconium tungstates, certain fused-silica formulations)

propositions.notes: 'Solid' alone is NOT a sufficient condition -- negative-thermal-expansion (NTE) solids exist. The gating condition is the expansion regime, of which 'ordinary metal' (K004m) is a subtype.

propositions.nl_gloss: Metals expand when heated (ordinary metals, positive-expansion regime).
propositions.notes: SPECIALIZATION of K004: ordinary metals are a subtype of the positive-expansion regime K004 quantifies over. Relation to K004: K004 ENTAILS K004m (context of K004m is SUBSUMED_BY K004's), not EQUAL. Used to test the 'specialization mistaken for identity' failure mode.

propositions.nl_gloss: Copper expands when heated.

context.temperature_domain: below copper's melting point, no phase transition

propositions.notes: SPECIALIZATION of K004m (Copper subtype_of Metal; NIST measurements confirm a positive expansion coefficient for copper across a substantial temperature range). K004m ENTAILS K004c, not EQUAL. This is the canonical 'false merge' trap case: a naive embedding-similarity canonicalizer will likely mark K004m and K004c EQUAL because the sentences are near-identical in surface structure.

propositions.nl_gloss: Density equals mass divided by volume.
propositions.notes: Definitional identity, always true, no context needed.

propositions.nl_gloss: Ideal gas law: PV = nRT.
propositions.notes: Fails for real gases at high pressure / low temperature -- context is load-bearing.

propositions.nl_gloss: Newton's second law: F = ma.
propositions.notes: Classic law; context excludes relativistic speeds and variable-mass systems (e.g. rockets).

propositions.statement: Boiling(x) <=> (Temperature(x) >= BoilingPoint(x, Pressure(x)) AND PhaseState(x) = liquid)
propositions.nl_gloss: A liquid boils when its temperature reaches the boiling point at the current pressure.
propositions.notes: Rule with an explicit conjunctive condition; used to test hyperedge/AND handling.

propositions.nl_gloss: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at 1 atmosphere of pressure.
propositions.notes: Instance fact, not a general law. Boiling point changes with pressure/altitude -- context is load-bearing.

propositions.nl_gloss: Electrical power equals current times voltage.
propositions.notes: Definitional; combines with K001 to derive K011 (see hyperedges.json) -- tests substitution-based ENTAILS, not surface EQUAL.

propositions.nl_gloss: Electrical power dissipated equals current squared times resistance.
propositions.notes: Derivable from K001 + K010 jointly by substitution (V=IR into P=IV) -- see hyperedges.json. Neither K001 nor K010 alone entails K011.

propositions.nl_gloss: An object's speed at an instant equals distance traveled divided by elapsed time, when speed is constant over that interval.
propositions.notes: True only when speed does not change during the interval; otherwise distance/time gives only the AVERAGE speed, not the instantaneous value at any particular moment. Distinct from Velocity (C20, a vector: displacement/time) -- K012 is scalar Speed. V012c drops the constant_speed qualifier -- classic dropped-context decoy.

propositions.nl_gloss: Heat added equals mass times specific heat times temperature change.
propositions.notes: Breaks down during phase transitions (latent heat dominates instead).

propositions.nl_gloss: For a fixed mass, escape velocity increases as radius decreases.
propositions.notes: escape_velocity ~ sqrt(mass/radius); monotonicity only holds at fixed mass.

propositions.nl_gloss: For a fixed mass of liquid water between about 4C and its boiling point, volume increases as temperature increases, at constant pressure.
propositions.notes: FIXED from v0-draft: predicate is Volume, not LinearExtent -- a liquid sample has no stable intrinsic linear dimension the way a solid rod does. Water has maximum density at ~4C, so volume increases with T above that point. See K016 for the 0-4C anomalous region -- deliberately constructed apparent-contradiction pair (see P05).

propositions.nl_gloss: For a fixed mass of liquid water between 0C and about 4C, volume decreases as temperature increases, at constant pressure.
propositions.notes: Anomalous expansion of water: density is maximal at ~4C (USGS), so volume falls while warming toward it from 0C. Surface form directly negates K015's direction, but both are true over disjoint temperature_domain windows -- an apparent contradiction created by erasing context, not a real one. This is the single most important test case in v0 (see P05).

propositions.nl_gloss: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge.
propositions.notes: Definitional identity.

propositions.nl_gloss: Metals are conductors.
propositions.notes: Ontological class fact (was mislabeled INSTANCE_OF in v0-draft; fixed to SUBTYPE_OF since Metal and Conductor are both classes, not an individual-to-class link) -- not a causal/quantitative law. Tests that the classifier doesn't force everything into MONOTONIC_* form.

propositions.nl_gloss: No material is both a metal and a semiconductor.
propositions.notes: Simplifying assumption for Benchmark-v0 (see C14's scope_note): real metallic/semiconducting behavior is a transport regime, not an eternal class property. Kept as a hard disjointness fact here for tractability. Supports resolving K002/K003 as COMPATIBLE with DISJOINT context, rather than CONTRADICTS (see P01, P13).

propositions.statement: Volume(x) is CONSERVED under uniform_scaling(x) iff shape unchanged
propositions.nl_gloss: Scaling an object uniformly changes its volume unless the shape is held exactly proportional in a way that keeps volume fixed (trivial/never in practice).
propositions.notes: Deliberately awkward/edge-case proposition to stress-test the classifier on a near-vacuous statement; expect low agreement -- included for calibration, not as a load-bearing fact.
